roles.name: Switcher & Livestream
roles.overview: The Switcher & Livestream operator runs the ATEM switcher and the YouTube livestream from one desk. During the week you check who is on cameras. On Sunday you arrive by 9:00 to set up and rehearse, go live at 10:15, call the shots to the camera team on headsets and cut the service, then save everything, update YouTube and shut down. A win is a stream confirmed live in YouTube Studio before the service, cuts that follow the worship and the preacher, and a recording saved in vMix every week.

sub: How long the closing slide stays up: to be confirmed.
steps.t: After the blessing, click the closing slide in the vMix inputs so it goes to the livestream.
Stop recording in vMix.
Stop streaming in vMix.
In YouTube Studio, open the live stream and choose edit title and description.

sub: Post-production is handled separately. YouTube takes about 12 to 24 hours before the stream is ready for it.

At 10:27 ProPresenter plays the countdown (ramp-up) video over the top.
Nothing to do while it plays. When ProPresenter clears it, your ATEM picture shows.
Have Front ready: medium close-up on the worship leader.

steps.note: Record every week. This is the step people forget.
steps.t: At 10:30, click Record in vMix.
Hold Front on the worship leader, medium close-up, for 5 to 10 seconds.
Then move across to a wide shot or an instrument shot.

Use every camera, multiple times, with multiple shots from each. Call the shots to the camera operators on headsets.

rules: Don't load a new setup file mid-service.
Don't try an untested transition. We use cuts only.
Don't update ATEM, vMix or computer software on a Sunday.
Don't change the stream settings or bitrate mid-stream.
Don't stop streaming in vMix during the service, except for an extended altar call.
Don't assume the stream is live without checking YouTube Studio.
Don't film people being prayed for at altar calls.

roles.name: Sound
roles.overview: The sound operator makes sure everyone in the room and online can clearly hear every word spoken and sung. You arrive before rehearsal to power up and line check, mix the band and speakers through the service, and shut the system down safely afterwards. A win on Sunday is a service where nobody notices the sound because it simply works.

steps.t: Turn off amps and powered speakers first.
Shut down the playback computer and the desk.

steps.note: This is the start-up order in reverse.
steps.t: Switch off main power last.

steps: Return every wireless mic to its home.
Put used batteries on charge.
Coil cables over-under and put them away.
down.title: Pack away mics and batteries

steps: Tell your team leader about any issue before you leave.

steps: Walk-in music playing at a comfortable level.
Host and pastor mics on, checked and muted until needed.
Band channels ready for the opening song.
live.title: Before the countdown

steps: Vocals sit on top of the band. Words matter most.
Watch the stage, not just the desk. Unmute before someone speaks, not after.

steps.note: The room is loud. The stream only hears the desk.
steps.t: Keep an eye on the stream mix as well as the room.

live.title: Quick mixing reminders

steps.t: Worship to host: bring up the host mic as the last song ends.
Host to sermon: bring up the pastor's mic and pull down band channels.
Sermon to response: bring the band back in gently as they start.
Switch on main power for the desk and stage boxes.

sub: Wait for the desk to fully load its show file before touching faders.
steps.t: Turn on the mixing desk and the playback computer.

steps.note: Speakers go on last and off first, so they never pop.
steps.t: Turn on amps and powered speakers last.

steps: Put charged batteries in every handheld and headset mic.
Confirm each receiver shows signal and battery level.

steps.note: Low batteries rarely die in rehearsal. They die in the sermon.
steps.t: Swap any battery showing two bars or less.

pre.title: Check batteries and wireless mics

steps.t: Ask each musician and vocalist to play or speak one at a time.
Confirm the signal lands on the correct channel and the label matches.
Note anything missing and fix it before rehearsal starts.
Have the person sing or play at their loudest normal level.

steps.note: Set gain at rehearsal volume, not soundcheck politeness. People always get louder.
steps.t: Raise the gain until the meter sits healthily without reaching the red.

steps: Build a rough front-of-house mix while the band runs the set.
Check every musician is happy with what they hear before rehearsal ends.
Save the scene once rehearsal is done.

rules: Don't power speakers on before the desk, or off after it.
